questions.question: In 2025, the Ministry of Defence unveiled a long-term roadmap emphasising future-generation technologies such as AI, hypersonic weapons, nuclear propulsion for warships, and next-generation combat systems. Which of the following is the name of this plan/roadmap?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Technology Perspective & Capability Roadmap 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Defence (MoD)** unveiled the **Technology Perspective & Capability Roadmap (TPCR) 2025** to provide the domestic industry with a clear vision of the future requirements of the **Indian Armed Forces**.
 
• The roadmap serves as a guiding document for **Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs)**, **DRDO**, and **private sector players** to align their **Research and Development (R&D)** efforts with the long-term needs of the military.
 
• It emphasizes the development of **Future-generation technologies**, specifically focusing on **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**, **Hypersonic Weapons**, and **Nuclear Propulsion** for naval vessels.
 
• The **TPCR 2025** is designed to reduce **import dependency** by fostering a robust **indigenous ecosystem** for **next-generation combat systems** and **autonomous platforms**.
 
• This document replaces or updates earlier versions like the **TPCR 2018**, reflecting the rapid changes in the **global security landscape** and the emergence of **asymmetric warfare** technologies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hypersonic Technology:** 
 
 
• These weapons travel at speeds exceeding **Mach 5** (five times the speed of sound).
 
• The **TPCR 2025** prioritizes the indigenous development of **Hypersonic Glide Vehicles (HGV)** and **Hypersonic Cruise Missiles** to enhance India's **strategic deterrence**.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Propulsion for Warships:** 
 
 
• Unlike conventional diesel-electric engines, **nuclear propulsion** allows **warships** and **submarines** to operate at high speeds for extended periods without the need for frequent refueling.
 
• This technology is crucial for the **Indian Navy** to maintain a persistent presence in the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)** and beyond.
 
 
 
• **Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Defence:** 
 
 
• The roadmap highlights the integration of **AI** into **command and control systems**, **predictive maintenance**, and **autonomous surveillance drones**.
 
• The **Defence AI Council (DAIC)** and **Defence AI Project Agency (DAIPA)** are central to implementing these objectives.
 
 
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat in Defence:** 
 
 
• The **Government of India** has set a target to achieve **defence exports** worth **INR 35,000 crore (USD 5 billion)** by **2025**.
 
• The **TPCR 2025** acts as a catalyst for the **Make in India** initiative by identifying **complex platforms** that can be built domestically.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Long Term Integrated Perspective Plan (LTIPP):** The **TPCR 2025** is derived from the broader **15-year LTIPP**, which outlines the long-term capability building of the **Army, Navy, and Air Force**.
 
• **iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence):** Launched in **April 2018**, this initiative supports **startups** and **MSMEs** in developing the high-end technologies listed in the roadmap.
 
• **Quantum Computing:** The roadmap also touches upon **Quantum Key Distribution (QKD)** and **Quantum Communication** to secure military networks against **cyber threats**.
 
• **Directed Energy Weapons (DEWs):** Future combat systems include **lasers** and **high-power microwaves**, which are mentioned as critical areas for **technological sovereignty**.
</ul

questions.question: Where was the Combined Operational Review and Evaluation (CORE) Programme organised by the Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) from 22 to 26 September 2025?

options.text: Defence Services Staff College, Wellington, Tamil Nadu
United Service Institution of India, New Delhi

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United Service Institution of India, New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Combined Operational Review and Evaluation (CORE)** Programme is a high-level tri-service engagement aimed at enhancing the strategic and operational synergy among the **Indian Armed Forces**.
 
• The programme was organised by the **Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS)** from **22 to 26 September 2025**.
 
• The venue for this prestigious event was the **United Service Institution of India (USI)**, located in **New Delhi**. This institution serves as a premier center for research into national security and defense matters.
 
• The primary objective of the **CORE Programme** is to provide a platform for senior military leadership to evaluate current operational doctrines and evolve a unified approach toward **future warfare** scenarios.
 
• It focuses on fostering **Jointness** and **Integration** across the **Indian Army**, **Indian Navy**, and **Indian Air Force** to ensure a cohesive response to national security threats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **United Service Institution of India (USI):**
 
 
• Established in **1870** by **Major General Sir Charles MacGregor**, the **USI** is one of India's oldest national security and defense think tanks.
 
• Located in **New Delhi**, it provides a venue for lectures, discussions, and research on military history, strategy, and international relations.
 
• It plays a critical role in professional military education and the development of strategic culture in India.
 
 
 
• **Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS):**
 
 
• **HQ IDS** was created on **October 1, 2001**, based on the recommendations of the **Kargil Review Committee**.
 
• It operates under the **Ministry of Defence** and is headed by the **Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee (CISC)**.
 
• Its primary mission is to promote "Jointness" for "Victory" by coordinating between the different branches of the military in planning, procurement, and training.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Significance of CORE:**
 
 
• The programme addresses modern challenges such as **Cyber Warfare**, **Space Defence**, and **Electronic Warfare (EW)**.
 
• It facilitates discussions on the transition toward **Integrated Theatre Commands**, which is a major reform intended to streamline command structures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Jointness and Integration:** The **CORE** programme is a step toward the goal of a fully integrated military force under the guidance of the **Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)**.
 
• **Future Warfare Training:** The curriculum of such programmes often includes **artificial intelligence (AI)** in combat, **drone technology**, and **asymmetric warfare** tactics.
 
• **Location Context:** While institutions like the **National Defence Academy (NDA)** in **Pune** and the **Indian Military Academy (IMA)** in **Dehradun** focus on initial officer training, the **USI** in **New Delhi** focuses on high-level strategic review and policy-level evaluation.
 
• **Role of CDS:** The creation of the post of **Chief of Defence Staff** in **December 2019** has significantly boosted the effectiveness of the **HQ IDS** in conducting such tri-service evaluations.
</ul

questions.question: ****In **August 2025**, **World Lion Day** celebrations in Gujarat were held at which **wildlife sanctuary**, where a major conservation and eco-tourism initiative was also highlighted?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Barda Wildlife Sanctuary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Lion Day** celebrations in **August 2025** were prominently held at the **Barda Wildlife Sanctuary** in **Gujarat**, marking a significant milestone in the expansion of the habitat for **Asiatic Lions**.
 
• During this event, the state government highlighted the progress of **Project Lion**, specifically focusing on the **Barda-Lion Safari** project, which aims to develop **Barda** as a secondary home for lions to reduce the concentration of the population in **Gir**.
 
• The initiative is designed to ensure the long-term genetic health and safety of the **Asiatic Lion** (Panthera leo leo) by creating a satellite population, which helps mitigate risks such as **Canine Distemper Virus (CDV)** or natural calamities.
 
• **Barda Wildlife Sanctuary**, established in **1979**, is located in the **Porbandar** and **Jamnagar** districts of **Gujarat** and is characterized by its hilly terrain and deciduous forest, similar to the **Gir National Park**.
 
• The eco-tourism initiative launched during the celebrations aims to boost the local economy of the **Saurashtra** region by attracting wildlife enthusiasts to the new safari area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Asiatic Lions:**
 
 
• The **Asiatic Lion** is slightly smaller than the **African Lion** and is distinguished by a longitudinal fold of skin running along its belly.
 
• Currently, their only wild population is found in the **Saurashtra** region of **Gujarat**, specifically in the **Gir National Park** and surrounding wildlife sanctuaries.
 
• In the **IUCN Red List**, they are categorized as **Endangered**, and they are protected under **Schedule I** of the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972** in India.
 
 
 
• **Project Lion:**
 
 
• Launched on the lines of **Project Tiger**, this program focuses on the conservation of the **Asiatic Lion** through habitat development, involvement of local communities, and modern technology in monitoring.
 
• The **"Lion @ 47: Visions for Amrit Kaal"** roadmap identifies **Barda Wildlife Sanctuary** as a crucial site for lion translocation and habitat restoration.
 
 
 
• **Geographic and Administrative Details:**
 
 
• **Barda Wildlife Sanctuary** covers an area of approximately **192 square kilometers**.
 
• It is situated about **15 kilometers** from the **Porbandar** coast, making it a unique coastal-hilly wildlife habitat.
 
• The forest type is predominantly **Southern Tropical Forest**, featuring species like **Babul**, **Gorad**, and **Khair**.
 
 
 
• **Other Sanctuaries in Gujarat:**
 
 
• **Pania Wildlife Sanctuary**: Located in **Amreli**, it acts as an extension of the **Gir** ecosystem.
 
• **Hingolgadh Wildlife Sanctuary**: Known as a premier **Nature Education Sanctuary** located in the **Rajkot** district.
 
• **Kutch Desert Wildlife Sanctuary**: One of the largest in India, famous for its **Flamingo City** and saline desert topography.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **World Lion Day** is celebrated globally on **August 10th** every year to raise awareness about the declining population of lions and the need for urgent conservation.
 
• The translocation of lions from **Gir** to **Barda** was recommended by the **Supreme Court** of India to prevent the extinction of the species from a single localized threat.
 
• The **Barda Safari** serves as a crucial link in the **Greater Gir** landscape, which now encompasses over **30,000 square kilometers** across several districts in **Gujarat**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following multilateral negotiations did India and the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) sign in August 2025 as a step towards a Free Trade Agreement (FTA)?

options.text: India-EAEU Terms of Reference (ToR) for an FTA

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India-EAEU Terms of Reference (ToR) for an FTA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **August 2025**, **India** and the **Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU)** took a significant step toward deepening economic integration by signing the **Terms of Reference (ToR)** for a **Free Trade Agreement (FTA)**.
 
• This document serves as the official framework and **roadmap** for negotiations, outlining the scope, sectors to be covered, and the timeline for the finalization of the trade deal. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **EAEU** is an influential economic bloc comprising five member nations: **Russia, Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan**.
 
• The signing follows a **Joint Feasibility Study** that highlighted the immense potential for trade growth between the two regions, particularly in manufacturing and services.
 
• The **ToR** is a prerequisite for formal institutional negotiations, marking a transition from preliminary discussions to structured legal and economic drafting of the **FTA**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU):**
 
 
• The **EAEU** was established to create a single market for goods, services, capital, and labor among its member states. It officially came into existence on **January 1, 2015**.
 
• The bloc represents a market of over **180 million people** with a combined **GDP** of several trillion dollars, making it a vital partner for **India's "Extended Neighborhood"** policy.
 
 
 
• **Trade Dynamics:**
 
 
• **India’s** trade with the **EAEU** has traditionally been dominated by **Russia**, but the **FTA** aims to diversify exports to other members like **Kazakhstan** and **Armenia**.
 
• Key sectors expected to benefit include **pharmaceuticals**, **agriculture**, **textiles**, **engineering goods**, and **information technology**.
 
 
 
• **Connectivity and Logistics:**
 
 
• A major component of this economic partnership is the **International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC)**, a **7,200-km** long multi-mode network of ship, rail, and road routes.
 
• The **INSTC** is designed to reduce the freight travel time between **India** and **Eurasia** by nearly **40%** and lower logistics costs by **30%**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Importance:** The **FTA** is seen as a strategic move by **India** to balance its trade portfolio and secure energy resources, as **EAEU** nations are rich in **oil, natural gas, and minerals**.
 
• **Regulatory Alignment:** The **Terms of Reference** include provisions for discussing **Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS)** measures and **Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT)** to ensure smooth customs clearances.
 
• **Timeline:** Following the **August 2025** signing, both parties have committed to fast-tracking the negotiations, with multiple rounds scheduled to address **tariff lines** and **Rules of Origin**.
 
• **Historical Context:** Formal interest in an **India-EAEU FTA** was first expressed in **2017**, and the **2025** signing represents the culmination of nearly eight years of diplomatic groundwork.

questions.question: Which of the following was launched by India in August 2025 to support countries of the Global South in meeting the Sustainable Development Goals?

options.text: Sustainable Development and Capacity Building Partnership

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India-UN Global Capacity Building Initiative**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **India-UN Global Capacity Building Initiative** was launched in **August 2025** as a strategic partnership between **India** and the **United Nations** to share **India's development experiences** and best practices with the countries of the **Global South**.
 
• This initiative is designed to support the achievement of the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** by providing a platform for **technical expertise** and knowledge exchange, specifically focusing on the **2030 Agenda**.
 
• The initiative aims to operationalize the development priorities identified during **India's G20 Presidency**, emphasizing the needs of **Developing Nations** and **Least Developed Countries (LDCs)**.
 
• It focuses heavily on the implementation of **Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI)**, which includes systems like **Aadhaar** and **Unified Payments Interface (UPI)**, to drive financial inclusion and social empowerment across the **Global South**.
 
• The program is implemented in collaboration with the **United Nations Office for South-South Cooperation (UNOSSC)** and **United Nations India**, ensuring a coordinated international effort to reach global targets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• Adopted by all **United Nations Member States** in **2015**, the SDGs are a collection of **17 interlinked global goals** designed to be a "blueprint to achieve a better and more sustainable future for all."
 
• The **India-UN Global Capacity Building Initiative** directly targets goals such as **Goal 1 (No Poverty)**, **Goal 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth)**, and **Goal 17 (Partnerships for the Goals)**.
 
 
 
• **Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI):**
 
 
• **DPI** refers to blocks or platforms such as **digital identification**, **payment systems**, and **data exchange** layers that help countries deliver vital services to their citizens.
 
• **India** has emerged as a global leader in **DPI**, using it to transfer **subsidies** directly to the bank accounts of millions, a model now being exported to other **emerging economies**.
 
 
 
• **Global South:**
 
 
• The term **Global South** broadly refers to regions within **Latin America**, **Asia**, **Africa**, and **Oceania** that are often characterized as **developing** or **underdeveloped**.
 
• **India** has positioned itself as the "Voice of the Global South," advocating for **debt restructuring**, **climate finance**, and **technology transfer** for these nations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Collaboration:** The initiative represents a deepening of the relationship between **India’s Ministry of External Affairs (MEA)** and the **UN** system to foster **South-South Cooperation**.
 
• **Implementation Framework:** It involves the creation of **capacity-building** workshops, **training modules**, and **policy advisory** services tailored to the specific geographical and economic contexts of the recipient countries.
 
• **History of Partnership:** This initiative follows the **India-UN Development Partnership Fund**, established in **June 2017**, which has supported numerous projects in **SIDS (Small Island Developing States)** and **Landlocked Developing Countries (LLDCs)**.
 
• **G20 Legacy:** The **New Delhi Leader’s Declaration** from the **2023 G20 Summit** served as the conceptual foundation for this initiative, emphasizing that **no one should be left behind** in the digital age.

questions.question: Thiyam Suryamukhi Devi, honoured with the Padma Shri in 2025, is famous for which classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipuri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thiyam Suryamukhi Devi** is a legendary figure in the realm of Indian classical dance, specifically renowned for her mastery of **Manipuri** dance.
 
• In **2025**, she was honored with the **Padma Shri**, one of India's highest civilian awards, in recognition of her distinguished service and contribution to the field of **Art**.
 
• She hails from the state of **Manipur** and has played a pivotal role in preserving the traditional **Raas Leela** and other devotional dance forms associated with **Vaishnavism**.
 
• As a veteran artist and guru, she has been associated with the **Jawaharlal Nehru Manipur Dance Academy (JNMDA)** in **Imphal**, where she trained generations of dancers in the intricate movements and spiritual essence of **Manipuri** culture.
 
• Her performance style is characterized by the **graceful**, **lyrical**, and **fluid** movements that define the **Jagoi** style, moving away from the more vigorous movements found in other classical forms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Manipuri Dance**:
 
 
• Originating from the northeastern state of **Manipur**, it is one of the eight primary **classical dances of India**.
 
• It is deeply rooted in **religious rituals** and depicts the **Radha-Krishna** love theme known as **Raas Leela**.
 
• A unique feature is the **Potloi** costume, a stiff cylindrical skirt worn by female dancers. It avoids sharp edges and jerky movements, emphasizing a **soft, rounded silhouette**.
 
 
 
• **Odissi**:
 
 
• This dance form originates from **Odisha** and is characterized by the **Tribhanga** posture (the three-fold bending of the body).
 
• It was traditionally performed by **Maharis** in temples like the **Jagannath Temple** in **Puri**.
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam**:
 
 
• Hailing from **Tamil Nadu**, it is considered the **oldest classical dance** form in India.
 
• It is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and complex **Mudras** (hand gestures). It was historically associated with **Devadasis**.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**:
 
 
• Originating from the **Kuchelapuram** village in **Andhra Pradesh**, it combines both dance and acting.
 
• It features the **Tarangam**, where a dancer balances on the rim of a **brass plate** while carrying a pot of water on their head.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Padma Awards 2025**: These awards are conferred by the **President of India** at ceremonial functions held at **Rashtrapati Bhawan**. The **Padma Shri** is awarded for "distinguished service" in any field.
 
• **Cultural Impact**: **Thiyam Suryamukhi Devi's** work extends beyond performance to the **documentation** and **academic preservation** of **Manipur's** indigenous performing arts.
 
• **Classical Status**: The **Sangeet Natak Akademi** currently recognizes **eight** classical dances: **Bharatanatyam**, **Kathak**, **Kuchipudi**, **Odissi**, **Kathakali**, **Sattriya**, **Manipuri**, and **Mohiniyattam**.
 
• **Sankirtana**: Related to **Manipuri** dance, this ritual singing, drumming, and dancing of **Manipur** is inscribed on the **UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**.
</ul

questions.question: Which customer segment is affected by ICICI Bank’s raised minimum balance requirement?

• The revision is set to be implemented starting from **1 August 2025**. This date acts as the primary threshold for determining which customers are affected by the new balance criteria.
 
• According to the bank's notification, the increased minimum balance requirement will apply **only to new savings accounts** opened on or after **1 August 2025**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Existing customers who established their accounts before the **August 2025** deadline are not impacted by this specific increase and will continue to follow the **Average Monthly Balance (AMB)** rules applicable at the time of their account opening. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The policy applies based on the **date of account creation** rather than the type of account ownership. Therefore, **joint account holders** are treated based on when the account was opened, not their status as joint holders. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

__
 
• **Average Monthly Balance (AMB):** This is a financial metric calculated by adding the **closing balance** of an account for every day in a month and dividing the total by the **number of days** in that month. Banks use this to ensure customers maintain a minimum level of funds to cover operational costs.
 
• **Branch Categorization:** Minimum balance requirements in **ICICI Bank** often vary based on the location of the branch, categorized as **Metro, Urban, Semi-Urban, and Rural**. While the revision mentioned applies to new accounts, the specific amount required still depends on these **geographical tiers**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **ICICI Bank:** Headquartered in **Mumbai**, it is one of the "Big Four" banks of **India**. It offers a wide range of banking products and financial services to corporate and retail customers through a variety of delivery channels.
 
• **Non-Maintenance Charges:** If a customer fails to meet the **minimum balance** criteria, the bank is entitled to levy **penal charges**. These charges are usually a percentage of the shortfall or a fixed fee as defined in the bank's **Schedule of Charges**.
 
• **Regulatory Oversight:** The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** mandates that all commercial banks must inform customers of any change in **service charges** or **minimum balance** requirements at least **one month** in advance to ensure transparency.

• **Effective Date:** The specific date of **1 August 2025** is critical for new applicants. Anyone opening an account starting this **year** and **month** must be aware of the higher liquidity commitment required by **ICICI Bank**.
 
• **Customer Communication:** Banks generally use **digital channels** like **SMS**, **Email**, and **mobile banking apps** to notify their users about such **policy updates** to comply with **fair practices**.
</ul

questions.question: In December 2024, which of the following schemes was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Haryana to promote financial literacy and insurance awareness among women?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bima Sakhi Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bima Sakhi Yojana** was launched by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** in **December 2024** during a high-profile event held in **Panipat, Haryana**.
 
• The primary objective of the scheme is to promote **financial literacy** and significantly increase **insurance awareness** among women, particularly those living in rural areas.
 
• The initiative aims to utilize the vast network of **Self Help Groups (SHGs)** across the country to drive the penetration of insurance products at the grassroots level.
 
• Under this scheme, selected women from these groups are trained to act as **Bima Sakhis**, who serve as insurance facilitators or point-of-sale persons to educate local communities and sell insurance policies. ***Hence, the option Bima Sakhi Yojana is the correct answer.***
 
• This launch is a strategic part of the government’s larger vision to empower women economically and achieve the goal of creating **3 crore Lakhpati Didis** (women members of SHGs earning an annual income of **Rs 1 lakh** or more).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Economic Empowerment**: By becoming **Bima Sakhis**, women can earn **commissions and incentives**, which provides them with a sustainable livelihood and enhances their **financial independence**.
 
• **Insurance Penetration**: India’s insurance density remains low in rural segments; this scheme addresses the "trust gap" by using local women as intermediaries who understand the local **socio-cultural dynamics**.
 
• **Lakhpati Didi Initiative**: Launched by the **Ministry of Rural Development**, this initiative focuses on diversifying the livelihood opportunities for women in **Self Help Groups** through various technical and financial interventions.
 
• **Role of IRDAI**: The **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** plays a crucial role in simplified regulatory frameworks to allow **Bima Sakhis** to operate efficiently without excessive bureaucratic hurdles.
 
• **Haryana's Role**: The state of **Haryana** has been a frontrunner in implementing women-centric rural schemes, making it a strategic location for the national launch of such a pivotal financial inclusion project in **2024**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Training and Capacity Building**: The **Bima Sakhis** undergo rigorous training modules covering the basics of **life insurance**, **general insurance**, and **health insurance** to ensure they can provide accurate information to villagers.
 
• **Social Security Linkage**: The scheme often facilitates enrollment in existing government insurance programs like the **Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)** and the **Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)**.
 
• **Digital Integration**: Most **Bima Sakhis** are equipped with digital tools or **mobile applications** to facilitate paperless transactions, aligning with the **Digital India** mission.
 
• **Target Demographic**: While the focus is on women, the ultimate goal is to provide **risk coverage** to the entire rural household, ensuring that families do not fall back into poverty due to unforeseen medical or accidental expenses.
</ul

questions.question: Which collection by Banu Mushtaq, translated by Deepa Bhasthi, won the International Booker Prize, 2025?

options.text: Under the Eye of the Big Bird

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heart Lamp**__.

__
 
• **Heart Lamp** is a celebrated collection of **short stories** originally written in the **Kannada** language by the veteran author and activist **Banu Mushtaq**.
 
• The work was translated into **English** by the noted writer and journalist **Deepa Bhasthi**, bringing the local nuances of **Karnataka** to a global readership.
 
• In a historic achievement for **Indian literature**, the collection was awarded the **International Booker Prize** in **2025**, recognizing the excellence of fiction translated into **English**.
 
• The stories in the collection predominantly revolve around the lived experiences of **Muslim women** in **South India**, particularly exploring themes of **gender politics**, **social justice**, and **religious identity**.
 
• The **International Booker Prize** win highlights the increasing global footprint of **regional Indian languages** and the vital role played by **translators** in cultural exchange.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Banu Mushtaq:**
 
 
• She is a prominent **Kannada** writer, **advocate**, and social activist based in **Hassan**, **Karnataka**.
 
• Her literary works are known for their **feminist** undertones and sharp critique of **patriarchal structures** within society.
 
• She has authored several influential books, including **Hada** (the original title of the winning collection) and **Benki Male**.
 
 
 
• **International Booker Prize:**
 
 
• This prestigious award is presented **annually** for a single book that is translated into **English** and published in the **UK** or **Ireland**.
 
• The prize aims to encourage more publishing and reading of quality fiction from all over the **world** and to promote the work of **translators**.
 
• The prize money of **£50,000** is shared equally between the **author** and the **translator**, emphasizing their equal contribution to the work's success.
 
 
 
• **Deepa Bhasthi:**
 
 
• She is an **independent writer** and **translator** whose work focuses on the intersections of **land**, **language**, and **identity**.
 
• By translating **Heart Lamp**, she has successfully preserved the **cultural idiom** and **linguistic flavor** of the original **Kannada** text for an international audience.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Literary Context:** **Kannada literature** has a rich history of over **1,500 years** and has produced some of India’s finest writers, including multiple **Jnanpith Award** winners. The **2025** win for **Heart Lamp** further cements its status in **world literature**.
 
• **Themes and Impact:** The book addresses **contemporary issues** such as **minority rights**, **educational empowerment**, and the **inner lives** of women, making it a significant contribution to **post-modern Indian fiction**.
 
• **The Original and Other Options:** While titles like **Hunchback** or **Under the Eye of the Big Bird** refer to other significant works in **Indian regional literature**, they were not the recipients of the **2025** prize mentioned in this context.
</ul

questions.question: How many runs did India’s women’s team score to set a national record in a One-Day International against Ireland in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**435**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **India Women’s cricket team** created history on **January 17, 2025**, by scoring a massive total of **435/4** in a **One-Day International (ODI)** against **Ireland**.
 
• This score of **435 runs** set a new **national record** for the **highest team total** by the **Indian Women's team** in the history of **ODI cricket**.
 
• The match was the **first ODI** of the three-match series, held at the **Niranjan Shah Stadium** in **Rajkot**, Gujarat.
 
• The innings featured a historic **double century** by star opener **Smriti Mandhana**, who scored **209 runs** off just **145 balls**, becoming the **first Indian woman** to reach the **200-run mark** in **ODIs**.
 
• Captain **Harmanpreet Kaur** also played a blistering knock, contributing **117 runs** off **61 deliveries**, which helped the team surpass the **400-run mark** for the first time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Previous Record:** Before this match, **India’s** highest total in **Women's ODIs** was **358/2**, which was also achieved against **Ireland** in **May 2017** during a quadrangular series in **South Africa**.
 
• **Smriti Mandhana’s Achievement:** With her **209-run** innings, **Smriti Mandhana** registered the **third-highest individual score** in **Women's ODI** history, trailing only **Amelia Kerr** (**232***) and **Belinda Clark** (**229***).
 
• **Partnership Record:** During this innings, **Mandhana** and **Kaur** shared a record-breaking **239-run partnership** for the **third wicket**, which is one of the highest in the history of the format.
 
• **Global Context:** While **435** is **India's national record**, the overall world record for the highest team total in **Women's ODIs** is held by **New Zealand**, who scored **491/4** against **Ireland** in **2018**.
 
• **Series Significance:** This match was part of the **ICC Women's Championship** cycle, which is crucial for **direct qualification** for the **2025 Women's Cricket World Cup**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Venue:** The **Niranjan Shah Stadium** (formerly known as the **Saurashtra Cricket Association Stadium**) in **Rajkot** provided a high-scoring pitch that facilitated several records during the **January 2025** series.
 
• **Match Result:** India won the match by a massive margin of **328 runs** after bowling out **Ireland** for **107**, marking one of their **largest victories** in terms of runs.
 
• **Statistical Milestone:** This was only the **fourth time** in **Women's ODI** history that a team managed to cross the **400-run** threshold, joining the ranks of **New Zealand** and **Australia**.
 
• **Smriti Mandhana** hit **26 boundaries** and **6 sixes** during her record-breaking knock, demonstrating a strike rate of over **144**.
</ul
